newsitem.title: CHINA: China August industrial output up 10.6 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: China August industrial output up 10.6 pct yr/yr.

text.p: China's industrial output rose by 10.6 percent to 150.3 billion yuan in August compared with the year-ago period, the State Statistical Bureau said on Monday.
Output rose by 12.2 percent year-on-year in July.

The August figure was the slowest monthly growth seen this year, and the bureau said that it reflected a continuation of operating difficulties in state enterprises and the effects of flooding in several regions of the country.
Output for the first eight months was 1.21 trillion yuan, up 12.9 percent over the same period of last year.

Output of companies wholly owned or majority controlled by the state was up a meagre 3.1 percent in August while output of collective and township enterprises grew by 17.5 percent and that of private enterprises rose 8.6 percent.

Light industry showed a gain of 11.6 percent while heavy industry was up 9.9 percent in August alone. Both figures were down from July's rate of increase of 13.9 percent for light industry and 10.9 percent for heavy industry.
Output growth in the first eight months was 13.2 percent for light industry and 12.5 percent for heavy industry.

The State Statistical Bureau also noted that the rate of sales to production reached its highest point for the year during the month, indicating a dwindling of unsold stockpiles. The rate of 96.08 percent was still below the rate for the same month last year, it said.
It said output of key items such as bicycles, sewing machines, televisions, air conditioners and freezers all showed declines in August.
Primary energy products and raw materials held steady during the month, the bureau said.
